notices.description: RFP is tailored specifically for parents/caregivers with a suspected or documented I/DD or cognitive delay that may impact their ability to safely parent. The ACS Developmental Disabilities Unit (DDU) partners with New York State Office for People with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD) providers to offer parenting skills training, one-on-one coaching, and linkages to supports and services for parents with a suspicion of and/or documented I/DD, including those with dual diagnoses of I/DD and other clinical needs. To be eligible for services, parents/caretakers must have a suspected or documented I/DD, some form of child welfare involvement, and reside within the five boroughs of New York City. OPWDD eligibility is not a pre-requisite for participation in the Essential Parenting Supports program. Contractors would assist parents with eligibility referral and OPWDD enrollment as needed. Regardless of OPWDD eligibility or enrollment status, parents would receive service coordination and linkages to community-based supports and services (e.g., adult Health Home). Essential Parenting Supports connects ACS-involved parents living with suspected or documented I/DD with parenting suppor…

notices.agency_name: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
notices.description: The New York City Department of Social Services (DSS) has adopted a new citywide approach to the Department of Homeless Services (DHS) response during Code Blue and Code Red weather emergencies. The new zone-based deployment model is designed to provide more consistent and comprehensive outreach coverage across areas with the highest likelihood of unsheltered individuals. Implementation of this model requires additional canvassing capacity beyond current DHS staffing levels. DSS/DHS is seeking to establish an on-demand staffing contract that can provide supplemental staff during emergency weather activations, particularly Code Blue and Red. These staffers would be responsible for going into the field, walking significant distances, engaging with street homeless individuals and encouraging them to come indoors. Staffers would also be assigned to cooling and warming buses to greet homeless individuals by accessing such buses, monitoring them, and offering connections to shelters. Moreover, DSS/DHS may add additional services and titles not included in this Negotiated Acquisition but necessary to complete servi…
notices.plain: The Human Resources Administration plans to award an on-demand staffing contract, through a negotiated acquisition, to supply extra outreach workers for Code Blue and Code Red weather emergencies to find and bring in homeless people; responses are due Nov. 17, 2026.

notable.agency_name: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
notable.description: The New York City Department of Social Services (DSS) has adopted a new citywide approach to the Department of Homeless Services (DHS) response during Code Blue and Code Red weather emergencies. The new zone-based deployment model is designed to provide more consistent and comprehensive outreach coverage across areas with the highest likelihood of unsheltered individuals. Implementation of this model requires additional canvassing capacity beyond current DHS staffing levels. DSS/DHS is seeking to establish an on-demand staffing contract that can provide supplemental staff during emergency weather activations, particularly Code Blue and Red. These staffers would be responsible for going into the field, walking significant distances, engaging with street homeless individuals and encouraging them to come indoors. Staffers would also be assigned to cooling and warming buses to greet homeless individuals by accessing such buses, monitoring them, and offering connections to shelters. Moreover, DSS/DHS may add additional services and titles not included in this Negotiated Acquisition but necessary to complete servi…
notable.plain: The Human Resources Administration plans to award an on-demand staffing contract, through a negotiated acquisition, to supply extra outreach workers for Code Blue and Code Red weather emergencies to find and bring in homeless people; responses are due Nov. 17, 2026.
